paragraphs.text: Shelah, Torah Shebikhtav, Shemos, Introduction §§2–6 — “I include all these portions under one heading, because they are joined in a leap year, when Israel are accustomed to awaken more strongly to the ways of repentance. Most earlier writers mentioned only the portions of Shovavim; later writers added Terumah and Tetzaveh. ... Had there been no diminution of the moon, there would never have been any intercalation, for if they had used one crown, their circuits and courses would have been equal. Now that they are separated, their courses and circuits are unequal, and seven intercalations must be made in the cycle to equalize the lunar years with the solar year, so that Pesach falls in spring and Sukkos at harvest-time. The intercalations arose through the accusation, which caused the accusation below that brings sin. Therefore a leap year is especially fitting for repentance.” The intervening paragraphs explain that the moon's accusation and diminution correspond above to the emergence below of the evil inclination and the accuser. Rav Tzadok first presents this explanation, then offers its complementary inversion: the very equalizing of moon and sun also anticipates the future restoration and therefore makes these days suitable for repentance.

paragraphs.text: Chullin 60b — “Seeing that the moon was not comforted, the Holy One, blessed be He, said: Bring an atonement for Me because I diminished the moon. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: Let this goat be an atonement because I diminished the moon.”

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Chaim of Volozhin, Nefesh HaChayim I, chapter 4, main text, paragraphs 7 and 10 — “The heart of a person, at the center of the body, gathers everything into itself, corresponding to the Holy of Holies at the center of the inhabited world, the Foundation Stone. Like it, the heart includes all the roots and sources of holiness. Our Sages alluded to this in the Mishnah in the chapter Tefillas HaShachar: 'He should direct his heart toward the Holy of Holies.' … Likewise, every sin and transgression through which a Jew brings foreign fire into his heart, through anger or other evil desires, is literally comparable to the verse, 'Our holy and beautiful house … has been burned with fire.' May the Merciful One save us.”

paragraphs.text: Connection: Nefesh HaChayim gives the inner sanctuary a precise structure: the heart corresponds specifically to the Holy of Holies, and destructive desires are its foreign fire. He draws the same inward implication from the direction of the heart in prayer that Rav Tzadok invokes here. This explains why repentance during Terumah and Tetzaveh must rebuild the heart's holiness, rather than merely recall the construction of a separate sacred building.

paragraphs.text: Kedushas Levi, Shekalim, s.v. Taam al Adar — “The reason that Adar sometimes comprises two months, as the intercalated month, is that the twelve months of the year correspond to the twelve tribes of God. Adar, whose constellation is fish, corresponds to Yosef, who is compared to fish over which the evil eye has no power, as Scripture says, Yosef is a fruitful son, a fruitful son above the eye. Yosef fathered two tribes, Menashe and Ephraim; therefore there are two Adars.”

paragraphs.text: Zohar II 166b–167a, Terumah — “In the same way, 'Torah is light': the Torah, given from the side of that primordial light, is continually sown in the world, producing offspring and fruit without ever ceasing; from its fruit the world is nourished.” The passage explicitly joins the gardener's primordial light to Torah's continuing fruitfulness. Rav Tzadok applies this to Ephraim, whose name expresses fruitfulness, and to the growth of Oral Torah after overcoming evil. The intervening discussion qualifies the garden's fruitfulness during exile.

paragraphs.text: Zohar II 137b, alternate text; Addenda II §8 — “In the mystery of 'Guard,' speech, night: this is 'the Torah of Hashem,' the Oral Torah. 'Moshe received Torah from Sinai and handed it to Yehoshua'—they explained this concerning the Oral Torah, for regarding the Written Torah it is written, 'Moshe commanded the Levites who bear the ark of Hashem's covenant ... Take this Torah scroll.' This was fitting for the Levites, for that which is bound to the sun. Moshe shone upon Israel for forty years, the sun in the daytime; 'the Torah of Hashem' is the entrance of Shabbos, in one mystery.” The original is preserved both in the alternate reading embedded in Terumah 16 and in the second volume's Addenda §8. The expanded Addenda wording explicitly includes the handing to Yehoshua. Rav Tzadok's identification of Yehoshua's book with the hidden roots of Oral Torah develops this precise distinction.

paragraphs.text: Pri Tzaddik, Chanukah §25, s.v. UvaGemara — “We have already said that 'Had Israel not sinned, only the five books of Torah and the book of Yehoshua would have been given to them, because it contains the apportioning of the Land of Israel' means that the book of Yehoshua is the secret of Oral Torah. 'Moshe received Torah from Sinai and handed it to Yehoshua' refers to Oral Torah, as the Zohar explains; he handed Written Torah to the Levites. Had they not sinned, they would have seen how everything is included in the five books of Torah, for nothing is absent from an allusion in the Torah. 'Its apportioning' means each Israelite's portion in Oral Torah, which is the Land, the aspect of the Congregation of Israel. Although the book of Yehoshua consists only of town names, the secrets of Oral Torah's roots are hidden in it, as it is the first book after Moshe's Torah.” This is the exact earlier authorial explanation to which the present maamar directs the reader. It clarifies how the geographical allotments can signify each soul's distinct portion in Oral Torah.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Vayechi 15 — “Yaakov put Efrayim before Menasheh, for to him the main thing was the holiness Hashem sends from His side… since he recognized that all is from Hashem, he put Efrayim first.” This gives Yaakov's reasoning in full. Even a person's own effort against the yetzer is Hashem's help, so he also blessed with “the God who shepherds me” before “the angel who redeems me.”

paragraphs.text: Midrash Tanchuma, Beshalach 2 — “With Yosef's ark went the Shechinah, the Ark, the priests, the Levites, and seven clouds of glory. Yosef's ark traveled with the Ark of the Testimony in the wilderness. The nations asked: What are these two arks? They answered: This is the ark of a dead man, and this is the Ark of the living One of the worlds. Does a dead man travel with the Ark of the living One of the worlds? They answered: This one fulfilled all that is written in that one.”

paragraphs.text: Rosh Hashanah 25b — “Scripture weighed three lesser figures like three greater figures, to teach you that Yerubaal in his generation is like Moshe in his generation; Bedan in his generation is like Aharon in his generation; Yiftach in his generation is like Shmuel in his generation. This teaches that even the least of the least, once appointed a leader over the public, is like the mightiest of the mighty.” The Gemara identifies Yerubaal with Gideon. Its direct subject is the authority of the appointed leaders of each generation; Rav Tzadok develops the spiritual meaning of the comparison.

paragraphs.text: Vayikra Rabbah 22:9 — “Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said: Seven transgressions were committed in Gideon's bull: wood of an asherah, disqualified stones, an animal designated for idolatry, a bull that had been worshipped, a non-priest, night, and an animal not yet of the required age.” The Midrash first establishes that a prophet can authorize an exceptional offering. Rav Tzadok contrasts this commanded episode with the unauthorized Golden Calf.

paragraphs.text: Temurah 28b — “Rava said: Indeed, they had worshipped it, and this was an exceptional ruling, as Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said: Eight things were permitted that night: offering outside the Sanctuary, night, a non-priest ...” The list continues on 29a: a service vessel, a vessel of an asherah, wood of an asherah, an animal designated for idolatry, and an animal that had been worshipped. The Bavli's eight permissions and the Midrash's seven transgressions have different enumerations; neither should be silently changed to match the other.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Maharsha, Chiddushei Aggados, Taanis 15a — “Rashi explains that the upright surpass the tzaddikim, but the Rashba wrote that the upright are a level below the tzaddikim.” Rav Tzadok follows Rashi's order. First comes the light sown for the tzaddik, the Torah she'b'al peh that repairs the yetzer; then, once the heart is wholly straightened, comes the higher gift of joy.

p: In the Torah we do not find joy
except where there is a mitzvah of it;
and regarding Shabbos it is stated (Sifrei, Behaaloscha 19):
"'And on the day of your joy' (Bamidbar 10:10) —
for though there is no mitzvah of joy on Shabbos,
in accepting the yoke of His Kingship, may He be blessed,
"I will put an end to all her rejoicing,
her festival, her new moon and her Shabbos...";
it is hinted that on Rosh Chodesh too
what place there is on Rosh Chodesh for joy.
that wherever there is a revelation of Atika,
meaning that Yisrael are bound to the root
they merit to make the heart upright,
and "for the upright of heart, joy."
And so it is stated in the holy Zohar
with which they praised the Holy One, blessed be He,
Alef was engraved in the darkness...,
And it is stated in the Gemara (Arachin 11a):
that is with joy and gladness of heart?
and the joy comes through the revelation of Atika,
which is in "Az," as mentioned above.
Shabbos has in it a revelation of Atika,
as they said in the holy Zohar
"So too at the renewals of the moon,
for the sun shines on it
through the light of Atika above";
we say the Kedushah of Keser
in the Mussaf of Rosh Chodesh;
אַךְ הַהֶאָרָה הוּא רַק לְפִי שָׁעָה
but the illumination is only temporary,
"Since it is called a festival, let him say it...;
a night sanctified for a festival
yet we say Hallel on Rosh Chodesh,
the custom of their fathers is in their hands";
that is, in Bavel they instituted
and this is because Bavel was the place of
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר מִשְׁפָּטִים מַאֲמָר א וּשְׁאָר מְקוֹמוֹת)
(as explained in Mishpatim, maamar 1, and elsewhere);
and therefore they sensed the hint
even on Rosh Chodesh, as mentioned above.
כֵּיוָן דְּעַל יְדֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
which is the "light sown for the tzaddik,"
one merits "for the upright of heart, joy,"
it emerges that on every Rosh Chodesh
there is a hint of joy,
And regarding the month of Adar we find (ibid. 29b):
that is, they are bound to the root
for mazal is that which is above
the grasp and intellect of man,
in the manner of what they said (Megillah 3a):
אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִינְהוּ לָא חָזוּ
"When Adar enters we increase in joy,"
just as joy and gladness are hinted
that Yisrael feel joy in it,
And when one merits, in Adar,
which was formed with the letter Kuf, "Kadosh,"
for the heart to be "My holy mountain,"
so that the heart becomes a Mishkan for the Shechinah,
וְלֹא יָרֵעוּ וְגוֹמֵר בְּכָל הַר קָדְשִׁי
and "they shall not harm... in all My holy mountain,"
toward the house of the Holy of Holies,
they are destined to be redeemed,
and on Shabbos Chol HaMoed Pesach
the Haftarah is the dry bones,
for on Pesach there will be the revival of the dead,
after all the blemish and the accusation are rectified,
and "the light of the moon will be
like the light of the sun."

paragraphs.text: ZoharIII 79b, Achrei Mos 74, s.v. Uf hachi — “So too at the renewal of the moon, for the sun shines upon her with the joy of the light of the Ancient One above. Therefore this offering is directed above, so that everything may be sweetened and joy be found in the world. Hence the words Bring an atonement for Me are exact.” The Zohar connects the renewed moon, the Rosh Chodesh offering, and supernal joy. This supplies Rav Tzadok's reason for finding an element of joy in Rosh Chodesh.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Arizal, Shaar HaKavanos, Derushei Rosh Chodesh 3 — “This explains why we say ‘Keser’ in the Mussaf of Rosh Chodesh as on Shabbos … whereas on Rosh Chodesh only the Nukva rises to the Keser of Z'eir Anpin.” The Arizal measures how much of Atika is revealed on Rosh Chodesh. The rise is real but partial, which is why its joy is only hinted.

paragraphs.text: Arakhin 10b — “Rosh Chodesh is called an appointed occasion, so let Hallel be recited! It is not sanctified through a prohibition of work, as it is written, The song shall be yours as on the night a festival is sanctified: a night sanctified as a festival requires song; one not sanctified as a festival does not require song.” This discussion concerns obligatory complete Hallel. It does not deny the separate custom of reciting an abridged Hallel on Rosh Chodesh.

paragraphs.text: Taanit 28b — “Rav came to Bavel and saw that they recited Hallel on Rosh Chodesh. He thought to stop them. When he saw that they skipped passages, he said: This shows that the custom of their ancestors is in their hands. A Sage taught: An individual should not begin; but if he began, he completes it.”

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Av 1 — “Then the light of the moon will be like the light of the sun… and the holiness of the month will be revealed… This custom began in Bavel; in Eretz Yisrael they did not.” Rav Tzadok adds that the full festival quality of Rosh Chodesh belongs to the future. Bavel's partial Hallel, with its skipped passages, reflects a holiness only partly grasped.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Hashanah 10 — “Mazla is the name for the root of the soul, which a person himself cannot grasp, as it says (Megillah 3a): ‘Even though they do not see, their mazal sees.’” This identifies the mazal that is “healthy” in Adar with the soul's own hidden root in Atika. Adar's joy therefore comes from a bond with Hashem that lies deeper than anything a person can perceive in himself.

paragraphs.text: Megillah 31a — “Rav Huna said in Rav's name: On a Shabbos occurring during Chol HaMoed, whether Pesach or Sukkos, we read See, You say to me. For the haftarah, on Pesach we read The dry bones; on Sukkos, On the day Gog comes.” The Gemara establishes the haftarah reading. Rav Tzadok connects its resurrection vision with Nisan; the quoted ruling does not itself state the date of the resurrection.
